easy.question: What does UI mean?
easy.answer: User Interface: everything the user sees and touches on a screen (buttons, menus, colours, text).

easy.question: What does UX mean?
easy.answer: User Experience: how easy and pleasant it feels to use a product, from start to finish.

easy.question: What do we call the letters' style and shape?
easy.answer: Typography: the choice of fonts, sizes, weights and spacing of text.

easy.question: What does "responsive" mean?
easy.answer: A responsive design adapts to different screen sizes: phone, tablet and computer.

easy.question: What do we call a button that encourages users to act?
easy.answer: A CTA (Call To Action), for example "Buy now" or "Sign up".

easy.question: Which colour is often used to show success?
easy.answer: Green, as in "Your message has been sent".

easy.question: Which tool is widely used to create UI designs and prototypes?
easy.answer: Figma, a collaborative design tool that runs in the browser.

easy.question: Which software is mainly used to create vector illustrations?
easy.answer: Adobe Illustrator.

easy.question: What do you call the first page of a website?
easy.answer: The homepage.

easy.question: What is the name of the menu at the top of a website?
easy.answer: The navigation bar (or navbar).

easy.question: What do we call a symbol used to represent an action?
easy.answer: An icon, for example a magnifying glass for "search".

easy.question: What is a clickable element that takes users to another page called?
easy.answer: A link (or hyperlink).

easy.question: What do we call a brand's symbol or graphic mark?
easy.answer: A logo.

easy.question: What file format is best for a logo with a transparent background?
easy.answer: SVG: a vector format that stays sharp at any size and supports transparency (PNG also works).

easy.question: What is the name of the small window that appears on top of a page?
easy.answer: A pop-up (or modal window).

easy.question: What format is commonly used for animated images?
easy.answer: GIF.

easy.question: What do we call the section at the bottom of a website?
easy.answer: The footer: it usually holds contact info, legal links and social media.

easy.question: What colour is often used for warning messages?
easy.answer: Orange (or yellow): it says "be careful" without meaning "error".

easy.question: What document explains how a brand should look?
easy.answer: Brand guidelines (or a brand style guide): logo, colours, fonts and tone of voice.

easy.question: How many seconds do users usually wait before losing patience with a slow website?
easy.answer: About 3 seconds. After that, many visitors leave.

hard.question: What is the space inside an element, between its content and its border, called?
hard.answer: Padding. (The space outside the border is the margin.)

hard.question: What is the practice of making a website usable for everyone called?
hard.answer: Accessibility: designing for all users, including people with disabilities (contrast, keyboard use, screen readers).

hard.question: What type of image can be resized without losing quality?
hard.answer: A vector image: it is made of shapes and maths, not pixels.

hard.question: What is the UX method of comparing two versions to see which works better?
hard.answer: A/B testing: version A and version B are shown to different users and the results are compared.

hard.question: What theory explains why we see nearby elements as a group?
hard.answer: The Gestalt principle of proximity: elements that are close together look related.

hard.question: What colour mode is mainly used for printing?
hard.answer: CMYK: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Key (black). In French: CMJN.

hard.question: What colour mode is used for digital screens?
hard.answer: RGB: Red, Green, Blue. In French: RVB.

hard.question: What do we call a fictional profile of a target user?
hard.answer: A persona: a made-up person with a name, goals and frustrations, based on real research.

hard.question: Which Figma feature automatically organises elements and adjusts spacing?
hard.answer: Auto layout: it works a bit like CSS Flexbox.

hard.question: What do you call the clickable version of a design used to test navigation?
hard.answer: An interactive prototype.

hard.question: What do you call the visual change when you move the mouse over an element?
hard.answer: A hover effect, for example a button that changes colour.

hard.question: What do we call the large introductory section at the top of a website?
hard.answer: The hero section: a big title, an image and usually a CTA.

hard.question: What is the 60-30-10 rule used for when designing a website?
hard.answer: Colour balance: 60% main colour, 30% secondary colour, 10% accent colour.

hard.question: What do we call the top section containing the logo and the navigation?
hard.answer: The header.

hard.question: How many main colours should a brand palette ideally have to stay consistent?
hard.answer: Between 3 and 5 main colours.

hard.question: What is the recommended minimum font size for body text on a website?
hard.answer: 16px.

hard.question: Which CSS unit is commonly used to make font sizes responsive?
hard.answer: rem: it is relative to the root font size (1rem = 16px by default).

hard.question: Which attribute describes an image for screen readers?
hard.answer: The alt attribute (alt text), for example alt="A goose wearing a top hat".

hard.question: Which Figma feature lets you create different versions of a component?
hard.answer: Variants, for example a button in primary, secondary and disabled versions.

hard.question: What do we call the empty space around and between elements in a design?
hard.answer: White space (or negative space): it lets the design breathe and improves readability.

easy.question: What do you need to unlock your phone or your computer?
easy.answer: A password or a PIN code (or your fingerprint / face).

easy.question: Should you share your password with your friends?
easy.answer: No. A password is personal and should never be shared, even with friends.

easy.question: What do we call unwanted emails, often advertising?
easy.answer: Spam.

easy.question: What does Wi-Fi give you access to?
easy.answer: The Internet, without a cable.

easy.question: Is "123456" a good password?
easy.answer: No! It is one of the most used passwords in the world and is cracked instantly.

easy.question: What should you do when you leave your computer?
easy.answer: Lock it (Windows + L on a PC, Ctrl + Cmd + Q on a Mac).

easy.question: What do we call a fake website that looks like a real one?
easy.answer: A phishing website: it copies a real site to steal your login or bank details.

easy.question: What do we call a bad program that can damage your computer?
easy.answer: Malware (for example a virus).

easy.question: What should you do if you receive a suspicious email?
easy.answer: Don't click anything. Delete it or report it.

easy.question: What do we call the name you use to log in?
easy.answer: Your username (or login).

easy.question: What do you do to enter your account on a website?
easy.answer: You log in (or sign in).

easy.question: What do you do to leave your account on a website?
easy.answer: You log out (or sign out).

easy.question: What do we call information about you, like your name or address?
easy.answer: Personal data.

easy.question: What do we call a code sent by SMS to confirm your identity?
easy.answer: A verification code (or one-time code).

easy.question: Can a real website ask for your password by email?
easy.answer: No, never. If an email asks for your password, it is a scam.

easy.question: What do we call a program that protects your computer against viruses?
easy.answer: An antivirus.

easy.question: What should you check before clicking on a link?
easy.answer: The URL (the real address of the link): is it the official website?

easy.question: What do we call fake prizes online, like "You won an iPhone!"?
easy.answer: A scam.

easy.question: What should a strong password contain?
easy.answer: Upper and lower case letters, numbers and symbols, and at least 12 characters.

easy.question: Who should you call if your computer is hacked at work?
easy.answer: The IT team (IT support), right away.

hard.question: What is phishing?
hard.answer: A trick where attackers send fake messages (email, SMS) that look real, to steal passwords or bank details.

hard.question: What is two-factor authentication (2FA)?
hard.answer: Logging in with two proofs: something you know (password) plus something you have (a code on your phone).

hard.question: What does HTTPS add compared to HTTP?
hard.answer: Encryption (TLS): data between the browser and the website cannot be read or changed by others.

hard.question: What is ransomware?
hard.answer: Malware that locks or encrypts your files and asks for money to unlock them.

hard.question: What is the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
hard.answer: Symmetric uses one shared key. Asymmetric uses a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt.

hard.question: What is a firewall?
hard.answer: A security system that filters network traffic and blocks unwanted connections.

hard.question: What is a VPN used for?
hard.answer: To create an encrypted tunnel for your Internet connection and hide your real IP address, for example on public Wi-Fi.

hard.question: What is a brute-force attack?
hard.answer: Trying every possible password combination until the right one is found.

hard.question: What is an SQL injection?
hard.answer: An attack where malicious SQL code is typed into a form to read or change a website's database.

hard.question: What is XSS (cross-site scripting)?
hard.answer: An attack that injects malicious JavaScript into a web page, which then runs in other users' browsers.

hard.question: What is a DDoS attack?
hard.answer: Distributed Denial of Service: thousands of machines flood a server with requests until it crashes.

hard.question: Why should passwords be hashed in a database?
hard.answer: So that even if the database is stolen, the real passwords cannot be read. A hash cannot be reversed.

hard.question: What is social engineering?
hard.answer: Manipulating people (not computers) to get information, for example pretending to be IT support on the phone.

hard.question: What is a zero-day vulnerability?
hard.answer: A security flaw that is not known by the developer yet, so there is no fix (patch) for it.

hard.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
hard.answer: Each user or program gets only the access it really needs, nothing more.

hard.question: What does the GDPR protect?
hard.answer: The personal data of people in the European Union (RGPD in French).

hard.question: What is a backdoor?
hard.answer: A hidden way into a system that bypasses normal login and security.

hard.question: What is the 3-2-1 backup rule?
hard.answer: 3 copies of your data, on 2 different types of storage, with 1 copy kept off-site.

hard.question: What is a botnet?
hard.answer: A network of infected computers controlled by a hacker, often used for DDoS attacks or spam.

hard.question: What is a CAPTCHA used for?
hard.answer: To check that the user is a human and not a bot, for example "select all images with traffic lights".

easy.question: What does SEO stand for?
easy.answer: Search Engine Optimisation: improving a website so it ranks higher in Google's free results.

easy.question: What does CTR stand for?
easy.answer: Click-Through Rate: the percentage of people who click after seeing an ad or a link.

easy.question: What is a backlink?
easy.answer: A link from another website to yours. Good backlinks help your SEO.

easy.question: What is retargeting?
easy.answer: Showing ads to people who have already visited your website, to bring them back.

easy.question: What is a conversion?
easy.answer: When a visitor does the action you want: buying, signing up, downloading...

easy.question: What is a landing page?
easy.answer: A page built for one campaign, with one single goal (one CTA).

easy.question: What is a lead?
easy.answer: A potential customer who has shown interest, for example by leaving their email.

easy.question: What is a keyword?
easy.answer: A word or phrase people type into a search engine, like "cheap running shoes".

easy.question: What is a newsletter?
easy.answer: A regular email sent to subscribers with news, content or offers.

easy.question: What is influencer marketing?
easy.answer: Working with content creators to promote a brand to their audience.

easy.question: What is organic traffic?
easy.answer: Visitors who come from unpaid search results (not from ads).

easy.question: What is cart abandonment?
easy.answer: When a visitor leaves a website with products still in their shopping cart, without buying.

easy.question: What is an upsell?
easy.answer: Offering the customer a better, more expensive version of what they want to buy.

easy.question: What is a hashtag used for?
easy.answer: Grouping posts on the same topic so people can find them, like #design.

easy.question: What does SEA stand for?
easy.answer: Search Engine Advertising: paid ads in search engines, like Google Ads.

easy.question: What is a testimonial?
easy.answer: A customer's opinion about a product or a brand, used to build trust.

easy.question: What is Google Analytics used for?
easy.answer: Measuring a website's traffic: how many visitors, where they come from, what they do.

easy.question: What are impressions in advertising?
easy.answer: The number of times an ad is shown on screen.

easy.question: What does B2C mean?
easy.answer: Business to Consumer: a company that sells directly to individuals.

easy.question: What does "viral" mean for content?
easy.answer: Content that is shared massively and very quickly.

hard.question: What is the difference between SEO, SEA and SEM?
hard.answer: SEO = free (organic) results, SEA = paid search ads, SEM = Search Engine Marketing, which covers both.

hard.question: How do you calculate the CPC?
hard.answer: Cost Per Click = total ad cost ÷ number of clicks.

hard.question: An ad gets 20,000 impressions and 400 clicks. What is its CTR?
Name the four steps of the AIDA model.
hard.answer: Attention, Interest, Desire, Action.

hard.question: What is a long-tail keyword?
hard.answer: A longer, very specific search phrase, like "red running shoes for women size 38": less traffic, but visitors who convert better.

hard.question: What is a KPI?
hard.answer: A Key Performance Indicator: a number used to measure if a goal is reached, like conversion rate or number of leads.

hard.question: A site has 5,000 visitors and 100 sales. What is its conversion rate?
What do TOFU, MOFU and BOFU mean?
hard.answer: Top, Middle and Bottom Of the FUnnel: discovering, considering, then buying.

hard.question: What is a lead magnet?
hard.answer: A free offer (ebook, checklist, discount) given in exchange for contact details.

hard.question: What does AARRR stand for?
hard.answer: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue: the "pirate metrics" funnel.

hard.question: What is ROAS?
hard.answer: Return On Ad Spend: revenue from ads ÷ cost of the ads.

hard.question: What does CPM mean?
hard.answer: Cost Per Mille: the cost for 1,000 ad impressions.

hard.question: What is the difference between upselling and cross-selling?
hard.answer: Upselling offers a better version. Cross-selling offers a complementary product (fries with your burger).

hard.question: What is customer lifetime value (CLV)?
hard.answer: The total revenue a customer brings to a company over the whole relationship.

hard.question: What is social proof?
hard.answer: Showing that other people trust you: reviews, testimonials, number of customers.

hard.question: What is a heatmap used for?
hard.answer: Seeing where users click, move their mouse and scroll on a page.

hard.question: What is the difference between owned, paid and earned media?
hard.answer: Owned = your own channels (site, socials). Paid = ads. Earned = free coverage (press, shares, word of mouth).

hard.question: What is a lookalike audience?
hard.answer: New people who look like your current customers, targeted by an ad platform.

hard.question: 1,000 people see a product and 200 add it to their cart. What is the drop-off rate?
hard.answer: 80% (800 people out of 1,000 did not add it).

hard.question: What does CRO stand for?
hard.answer: Conversion Rate Optimisation: improving a site so more visitors take action.

easy.question: What does HTML stand for?
easy.answer: HyperText Markup Language: the language that structures the content of a web page.

easy.question: What does CSS stand for?
easy.answer: Cascading Style Sheets: the language that styles a web page (colours, fonts, layout).

easy.question: Which HTML tag is used for the main title of a page?
Which HTML tag creates a link?
easy.answer: <a>, with the href attribute: <a href="...">.

easy.question: Which HTML tag displays an image?
easy.answer: , with the src and alt attributes.

easy.question: Which HTML tag creates a paragraph?
Which CSS property changes the colour of the text?
easy.answer: color.

easy.question: Which CSS property changes the background colour?
easy.answer: background-color.

easy.question: Which language makes a web page interactive?
easy.answer: JavaScript.

easy.question: What is a web browser?
easy.answer: A program used to visit websites, like Chrome, Firefox or Safari.

easy.question: What does URL stand for?
easy.answer: Uniform Resource Locator: the address of a web page.

easy.question: What is a domain name?
easy.answer: The readable name of a website, like google.com.

easy.question: What is a database?
easy.answer: An organised collection of data, stored so it can be easily searched and updated.

easy.question: In a database table, what do we call one row?
easy.answer: A record (one line of data, for example one user).

easy.question: In a database table, what do we call one column?
easy.answer: A field (one type of information, for example "email").

easy.question: What does SQL stand for?
easy.answer: Structured Query Language: the language used to talk to relational databases.

easy.question: Which SQL command is used to read data from a table?
easy.answer: SELECT, for example SELECT * FROM users;

easy.question: What is an algorithm?
easy.answer: A list of step-by-step instructions to solve a problem, like a cooking recipe.

easy.question: What is a bug?
easy.answer: An error in a program that makes it behave in the wrong way.

easy.question: What does "front-end" mean?
easy.answer: The part of a website the user sees and interacts with (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).

hard.question: What is the difference between a class and an id in CSS?
hard.answer: A class (.name) can be used on many elements. An id (#name) must be unique on the page.

hard.question: What is the CSS box model?
hard.answer: Every element is a box made of content, padding, border and margin.

hard.question: Name the two main CSS layout systems used to align elements.
hard.answer: Flexbox (one direction: row or column) and Grid (two directions: rows and columns).

hard.question: What is a media query?
hard.answer: A CSS rule that applies styles only for some screen sizes, for example @media (max-width: 768px).

hard.question: What does "semantic HTML" mean?
hard.answer: Using tags that describe their meaning, like <header>, <nav>, <article>, <footer>, instead of only <div>.

hard.question: What is the DOM?
hard.answer: Document Object Model: the tree of HTML elements that JavaScript can read and change.

hard.question: What is the difference between GET and POST?
hard.answer: GET asks for data (visible in the URL). POST sends data to the server (in the request body), for example a form.

hard.question: What does a 404 status code mean?
hard.answer: Not Found: the page you asked for does not exist on the server.

hard.question: What is an API?
hard.answer: Application Programming Interface: a way for two programs to talk to each other and exchange data.

hard.question: What is the difference between front-end and back-end?
hard.answer: Front-end runs in the browser (what users see). Back-end runs on the server (logic, database).

hard.question: What is a primary key?
hard.answer: A column that uniquely identifies each row of a table, often an id.

hard.question: What is a foreign key?
hard.answer: A column that refers to the primary key of another table, to link the two tables.

hard.question: What is a JOIN in SQL?
hard.answer: A command that combines rows from two tables using a related column.

hard.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows?
hard.answer: WHERE, for example SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > 18;

hard.question: What does CRUD stand for?
hard.answer: Create, Read, Update, Delete: the four basic operations on data (INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE in SQL).

hard.question: Give an example of a one-to-many relationship in a database.
hard.answer: One customer can have many orders, but each order belongs to one customer.

hard.question: What is a loop in an algorithm?
hard.answer: A block of instructions repeated several times, for example a for or while loop.

hard.question: What is a condition in an algorithm?
hard.answer: An if / else test: the program does something different depending on whether it is true or false.

hard.question: What is the difference between a linear search and a binary search?
hard.answer: Linear checks items one by one. Binary works on a sorted list and cuts it in half at each step, so it is much faster.

hard.question: What is a function in programming?
hard.answer: A reusable block of code with a name, which can take parameters and return a result.
